methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $200M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Sublime Systems is a Series B climate & energy company founded by Leah Ellis and Yet-Ming Chiang that has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), supplemented by a broader climate-tech universe of nine private firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $200M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $380M. Peer-median analysis across the three directly comparable companies produces $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. The median valuation across both methods is $690M, with a low-end estimate of $323M and a high-end of $1.1B.

The wide dispersion between methods—stage-progression at the lower bound and peer-median at upper quartile—reflects material uncertainty in comparable selection and stage-equivalency assumptions. The peer set exhibits significant heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital efficiency. A defensible valuation range of $690M median (with bounds of $323M–$1.1B) is supported by the data, though further diligence on burn rate, unit economics, and regulatory pathway relative to named peers would sharpen this estimate.
